title: Social Democracy, Christian Democracy, Constitutional Structure, and the Welfare State
abstract: First solid support for the state-centered perspective in quantitative welfare state analysis. Shows contrasting effects of Christian democratic and social democratic governance on welfare effort, and strong effect of constitutional structure.

title: Politics and Inequality in Latin America and the Caribbean
abstract: First pooled time-series analysis of political and policy determinants of inequality in 18 Latin American and Caribbean countries 1970-2000.

title: Social Investment in Latin America
publication: The World Politics of Social Investment Volume I
abstract: Social investment and neoliberal legacies in Latin America. Examines whether LA states can break with neoliberal legacies through social investment strategies.

title: The Political Foundations of State Effectiveness
abstract: State effectiveness requires both bureaucratic capacity AND deliberative state-society relations (Sen-Ostrom model). Effective states ≠ simply strong states.

title: The Paradoxes of Contemporary Democracy: Formal, Participatory, and Social Dimensions
abstract: Examines tensions between formal democratic institutions and substantive equality. State's role in enabling or constraining participatory and social dimensions of democracy.

title: Distribution and Redistribution in Postindustrial Democracies
abstract: Analyzes the determinants of distribution and redistribution in postindustrial democracies using Luxembourg Income Study data.

title: Income Inequality and Redistribution in Post-Industrial Democracies: Demographic, Economic and Political Determinants
abstract: Examines state's redistributive role through welfare transfers and taxation. Welfare state generosity is primary mechanism translating politics into lower inequality.

title: Politics, Policies, and Poverty in Latin America
abstract: Analysis of the politics of poverty reduction in Latin America, examining how democracy and left government affect poverty outcomes.

title: Models of Capitalism: Lessons for Latin America
abstract: Edited volume examining different models of capitalism and their applicability to Latin America. Includes Huber introduction and conclusion, plus Stephens chapter on welfare state regimes.

title: Postindustrial Social Policy
abstract: Analyzes welfare state adaptation in postindustrial contexts. Shifts in social policy driven by deindustrialization, labor market dualization, and changing partisan coalitions.

title: Do Social Investment Policies Produce More and Better Jobs?
publication: Towards a Social Investment Welfare State?
abstract: Examines whether social investment policies (education, training, childcare) produce better employment outcomes in 17 OECD countries 1972-1999.

title: The Changing Shapes of Latin American Welfare States
abstract: Comprehensive overview of Latin American welfare state transformations over the past half century, from ISI era through neoliberal reforms to left turn expansion.

title: Predistribution and Redistribution: Alternative or Complementary Policies?
abstract: Argues predistribution and redistribution are complementary, not alternative approaches. Social investment and traditional redistribution both needed.

title: Revisiting Capitalist Development and Democracy
abstract: Retrospective on Capitalist Development and Democracy 30 years later. Argues fundamental arguments still hold but ongoing capitalist transformations vindicate their contention about erosion of class-party linkages.

title: Some Reflections on New Directions in Democracy Research
abstract: Huber's solo essay arguing for historically grounded configurative analyses over large-N average effects, closer dialogue between quantitative and comparative historical studies.

title: Power Resources Theory and Distributive Outcomes
abstract: Traces PRT from 1970s origins through modifications, reviews quantitative evidence evolution, compares explanatory power to institutional and ideas-based approaches. Tests whether PRT holds in the knowledge economy.

title: Successful Social Policy Regimes? Political Economy, Politics, and Social Policy in Argentina, Chile, Uruguay, and Costa Rica
abstract: Comparative analysis of the four most advanced social policy regimes in LA. State capacity to design, fund, and implement social policy is a key differentiator.

title: Goodbye to Meltzer-Richard: Testing Major Theories of Redistribution
abstract: Re-analyzes four major redistribution theories using comprehensive 589 country-year dataset 1963-2019. Finds partisan governments and welfare generosity are directly related to redistribution. Refutes Meltzer-Richard model.

title: Challenging Inequality: Variation across Postindustrial Societies
abstract: Full book analyzing how welfare state generosity remains the most important factor shaping redistribution in 22 postindustrial countries. Statistical + comparative historical analysis of Germany, Spain, Sweden, US.

title: The European Social Model under Pressure
publication: The European Social Model under Pressure
abstract: Chapter analyzing pressures on the European social model from globalization, deindustrialization, and austerity.

title: Predistribution and Redistribution Working Paper
abstract: Working paper version of the predistribution/redistribution argument.

title: Capitalist Development and Democracy (Latin America chapter)
abstract: Latin America chapter from the landmark 1992 book establishing the three power clusters framework: class power, transnational power, state power.

title: The Bourgeoisie and Democracy: Historical and Contemporary Perspectives
abstract: Examines the historical role of the bourgeoisie in creating and maintaining political democracy, challenging the liberal view that the bourgeoisie was the main agent of democratization.

title: Capitalist Development and Democracy: The Controversy
abstract: Methodological chapter discussing the controversy between comparative historical and cross-national statistical approaches to studying capitalist development and democracy.

title: Internationalization and the Social Democratic Model: Crisis and Future Prospects
abstract: Analyzes whether globalization undermines the social democratic welfare state model. Examines state's capacity to sustain generous social provisions under economic internationalization.

title: Partisan Governance, Women's Employment, and the Social Democratic Service State
abstract: Introduces the concept of the social democratic service state — state as direct PROVIDER of welfare services. Feedback loop: public services → women's employment → demand for more services.

title: Introduction (Development and Crisis of the Welfare State)
publication: Development and Crisis of the Welfare State
abstract: Introduction to the landmark book on welfare state development. Partisan politics is the single most important factor shaping welfare state variation.

title: Theoretical Framework and Methodological Approach
publication: Development and Crisis of the Welfare State
abstract: Theoretical chapter elaborating the power resources framework, production regimes, and constitutional structure as determinants of welfare state development.

title: The Politics of Welfare States after the Golden Age: A Comparative Historical Analysis
publication: Development and Crisis of the Welfare State
abstract: Analyzes retrenchment and adaptation of welfare states in the post-Golden Age era. Examines vulnerability of different program types.

title: Conclusion (Development and Crisis of the Welfare State)
publication: Development and Crisis of the Welfare State
abstract: Conclusion summarizing partisan effects on welfare state development. Social democratic vs. Christian democratic vs. liberal welfare state configurations.
